pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/e2e/worker_lifecycle.rs:561 The structural pin that claims all four gate/hook calls sit inside `finalize_fanout` ends the function at the next column-0 bare `fn ` (worker.rs:1577 `vcr_params`), so its window also covers `publish_running` (1465) and `finish_from_executor` (1493); a call moved into the remote-finish path would stay green, which is the instrument-defaults-toward-green failure the technique names.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/e2e/worker_lifecycle.rs:561 The needles are good: they carry argument lists, and an exactly-once count makes a prose mention go red. The scope predicate is the problem: it reads 'next bare fn' rather than the construct's own end, so `pub(crate) fn` and `pub(crate) async fn` items are swallowed into the window.

crates/server/src/e2e/worker_lifecycle.rs:350 The per-app cap claim is proved by counting the peak number of runs in flight, with stubs held until `want` of them overlap. The run_one seam drains the fan-out as a synchronization point, not a deadline poll (worker.rs:236-237).
crates/server/src/e2e/worker_lifecycle.rs:410 A control test proves the harness itself is not serialising, so a peak of 1 under cap 1 is evidence about the cap, not an artifact of the harness.
crates/server/src/e2e/panic_containment.rs:36 The competing producer (the reaper) is armed, and the test asserts that the error text names panic containment rather than the reaper's message.
